questions.prompt: Why does JavaScript need asynchronous code at all, and what exactly does await pause?

keyPoints.text: Programs constantly wait on slow things: network, timers, user input, files.
keyPoints.quote: JavaScript often waits for things: network requests, timers, user input, file reads.

keyPoints.text: Rather than block, the runtime schedules the follow-up work for later.
keyPoints.quote: Instead of blocking everything, JavaScript schedules follow-up work.

keyPoints.text: A promise stands for a value that is not available yet.
keyPoints.quote: Promises represent values that may be available later.

keyPoints.text: async/await reads more cleanly but you still have to understand how promises flow.
keyPoints.quote: `async/await` improves readability, but it does not replace the need to understand promise flow.

keyPoints.text: await suspends only the async function it is in; the rest of the program keeps running.
keyPoints.quote: `await` pauses only inside the current async function, not the entire program.

questions.prompt: Walk through the loadPosts UI flow and explain why it checks response.ok before parsing.

keyPoints.text: It sets a loading message before the request starts.
It turns a non-OK HTTP status into a thrown error carrying the status code.
keyPoints.quote: throw new Error(`Request failed with status ${response.status}`);

keyPoints.text: Beginners assume fetch throws on every failed status; it does not.
keyPoints.quote: A common beginner mistake is assuming `fetch` throws on every failed HTTP status.

keyPoints.text: fetch rejects only when the network itself fails.
A 404 or 500 resolves normally, so the ok check is mandatory.
keyPoints.quote: A `404` or `500` still resolves, so you must check `response.ok`.

keyPoints.text: Any failure ends in a clear error message for the user instead of a silent stall.

questions.prompt: Explain how the wait(ms) helper turns a timer into a promise, and why this matters for real job work.

keyPoints.text: wait returns a new promise instead of the timer handle.
The promise's resolve function is the timer callback, so the promise settles when the delay ends.
Callers can chain on it like any other async result.
It is simply the promise form of a delay.
keyPoints.quote: This is the promise version of a delay.

keyPoints.text: Writing small custom promises demystifies other async patterns.
keyPoints.quote: Understanding simple custom promises makes other async patterns less mysterious.

keyPoints.text: Everyday app work (fetching, spinners, retries, forms, sync) rests on these ideas.
keyPoints.quote: Data fetching, loading spinners, retries, form submission, and state synchronization all depend on these ideas.
